chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
There is no harm in a menstruating woman and a junub reciting the Qur'an.

key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: a person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْقُرْآنَ: the Qur'an, the revealed scripture being recited
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection; a formula indicating permissibility

ai.seo_question: Can a menstruating woman or a junub recite the Qur'an in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling that it is permissible for a menstruating woman and a person in the state of janabah to recite the Qur'an. It addresses a matter of ritual purity and clarifies that Qur'an recitation itself is not prohibited for them.
